title: Classification / Odd One Out — In-Depth Guide — Part 13 of 16

questions.question: What does 'Nested Shapes' classification test?
options: Whether a group of figures share a consistent pattern of shapes nested inside one another, with one breaking it
questions.rationale: This tests whether figures share a consistent nested-shape structure, identifying the figure whose nesting pattern differs.

questions.question: What does the 'Symmetry Method' add to non-verbal classification, building on earlier methods?
options: Nothing new, it repeats the counting method
A dedicated check for whether each figure shares a consistent type/degree of symmetry
questions.rationale: The symmetry method specifically checks for consistent symmetry properties across figures, complementing the counting, position, and orientation methods covered earlier.

questions.question: What does 'Classification Using Graphs' apply to this domain?
options: Modeling items and their shared/differing properties as a graph, similar to other structured reasoning topics
A method with no structural basis
questions.rationale: This applies the same graph-based modeling idea used elsewhere in reasoning — representing items and their property relationships as connected nodes and edges.

questions.question: What does 'Classification and Invariants' focus on?
options: Properties that always change between items
Properties that remain constant (invariant) across the group, which is what defines the shared rule
questions.rationale: This focuses on invariants — properties that stay constant across the group — since it's exactly this constancy that defines the shared classification rule.

questions.question: What does an 'Invariant Diagram' help visualize?
options: Which properties remain constant across a group and which one item breaks that constancy
questions.rationale: An invariant diagram visually maps which properties stay constant across the group, helping pinpoint exactly where the one exception breaks that pattern.

questions.question: What does the 'Advanced Classification Strategy' likely consolidate?
options: Multiple techniques (feature vectors, invariants, graphs) combined into a more powerful, flexible solving approach
A strategy with no defined structure
questions.rationale: This consolidates the more advanced techniques covered — feature vectors, invariants, graph modeling — into a combined, more powerful and flexible solving approach.

questions.question: What does an 'Outlier Score' represent?
options: A quantitative measure of how much an item differs from the rest of the group, used to identify the most likely exception
questions.rationale: An outlier score quantitatively measures how much each item diverges from the rest of the group, helping identify the most likely true exception.

questions.question: What does a 'Cluster Model' apply to classification?
options: Grouping items by shared properties into clusters, where the outlier is the item that doesn't fit well into the main cluster
A model with no grouping concept
questions.rationale: This applies clustering directly to classification: items naturally group by shared properties, and the outlier is whichever item doesn't fit well into the main cluster.

questions.question: What does 'Hierarchical Classification' test?
options: Whether a group of items share a common level or position within a hierarchy, with one item at a different hierarchical level
questions.rationale: This tests whether items share a common position or level within a hierarchy, identifying the item positioned at a different level.

questions.question: What does 'Category-Level Matching' check for?
options: That all items have the same name
That items are compared at the same level of categorical specificity (e.g., all species names, not mixing species with genus)
A check with no practical use
questions.rationale: This ensures items are compared at a consistent level of categorical specificity, avoiding the error of mixing a more general category term with more specific ones.
